info.name: FHIR REST API
info.description:
End-to-end tests for the Python FastAPI FHIR R5 REST server.

Run the full collection in order â€” Auth registers a unique user and saves a Bearer token, which all subsequent requests inherit. The Patient folder creates a resource whose ID is stored in `patientId`. The Sort folder seeds additional patients to verify `_sort` ordering. The Include / RevInclude folder seeds a fresh patient and observation to test `_include` / `_revinclude`, saving their IDs to `includePatientId` and `includeObsId`. The Reference Validation folder verifies that dangling local references are rejected with 422. The _format Negotiation folder tests `?_format` parameter support (JSON accepted, XML â†’ 406). The Conditional Create folder tests the `If-None-Exist` header (0 matches â†’ 201, 1 match â†’ 200, 2+ â†’ 412). The $everything folder tests `GET /<resource>/{id}/$everything`. The Transaction / Batch Bundle folder tests `POST /` bundle processing. The _summary / _elements folder tests response shaping via `?_summary` and `?_elements`. The _lastUpdated folder tests date-prefix search via `?_lastUpdated`. The $validate folder tests `POST /{type}/$validate` without persisting.

**Base URL:** `https://localhost:443`
**Auth:** JWT Bearer (token saved automatically after Login)

item.name: Public
item.description: Unauthenticated endpoints. No Authorization header required. Use these to verify the server is running before attempting any authenticated requests.

item.name: Auth
item.description: User registration and login. Register generates a unique username (`alice_<timestamp>`) to avoid conflicts on repeated runs. Login saves the returned JWT to the `token` collection variable, which all protected requests use via `Bearer {{token}}`.

exec: // Fire 4 extra bad-password requests so the 5th (this request) triggers lockout.
pm.sendRequest({url: loginUrl, method: 'POST', header: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: {mode: 'raw', raw: body}}, () => {});

item.name: Patient
item.description: Full CRUD lifecycle for a Patient resource. Create saves the new resource ID to `patientId`, which Read, Update, Patch, and Delete all reference. Run these in order: Create â†’ Read â†’ Search â†’ PUT â†’ PATCH â†’ Delete. The DELETE at the end tombstones the resource so History requests can demonstrate the deleted version.

item.name: History
item.description: Version history interactions. Reads instance, type, and system history bundles. Run after the Patient CRUD folder — the patient will have been created, updated twice (PUT + PATCH), and deleted, so the history bundle should contain at least 3 entries. Version 1 may return 410 Gone after the DELETE. Pagination is supported via ?_count and ?_offset on all history endpoints; total always reflects the full history regardless of the page size.

exec: pm.test('Total reflects full history not just the page', () => {
pm.test('Next link present when history has more entries', () => {

item.name: Observation
item.description: Search interactions for Observation resources. Demonstrates subject reference filtering, LOINC code filtering, date range filtering with `ge`/`le` prefixes, and pagination via `_count`/`_offset`. These requests return empty bundles if no Observations have been created â€” that is still a valid 200 searchset response.

item.name: Condition, AllergyIntolerance, MedicationRequest
item.description: Search interactions for common clinical resources linked to the patient. All three filter by subject/patient reference using `patientId`. Empty bundles are expected unless matching resources have been created separately â€” the tests only assert on the Bundle structure, not entry count.

item.name: Sort
item.description: Validates `_sort` query parameter support. Two seed patients (Adams and Carter) are created first to guarantee the result set contains sortable data. All three sort requests use `_count=10` to avoid fetching thousands of records. Assertions check relative ordering of consecutive entries rather than hardcoded names, so they pass regardless of what other data is in the database.

exec: pm.test('First two entries are sorted family ascending', () => {
const entries = pm.response.json().entry.filter(e => e.resource && e.resource.name && e.resource.name[0].family);
pm.test('First two entries are sorted family descending', () => {
const entries = pm.response.json().entry.filter(e => e.resource && e.resource.name && e.resource.name[0].family);

item.description: Tests for `_include` and `_revinclude` query parameters. Seeds a fresh Patient (`includePatientId`) and Observation (`includeObsId`) first, then verifies that `_include=Observation:subject` appends the referenced Patient to the Bundle and `_revinclude=Observation:subject` appends linked Observations to a Patient search. Depends on: Auth (token).

exec: pm.test('No include entries with wrong target type', () => {

Reference Validation
item.description: Verifies that `before_create` / `before_update` hooks reject dangling references with 422 Unprocessable Content. Tests Observation (subject), Condition (subject), and AllergyIntolerance (patient). The happy-path request reuses `includePatientId` set by the Include folder â€” run Include first, or manually set the variable to a live Patient ID.

exec: pm.test('Status is 201 (absent subject is not validated)', () => {

item.name: _format Negotiation
item.description: Tests the FHIR R5 ?_format query parameter (Â§3.1.2). JSON variants (application/fhir+json, json, application/json) pass through normally. XML and unknown formats return 406 OperationOutcome with issue code not-supported. Format negotiation runs before authentication â€” an unauthenticated request with an unsupported _format returns 406, not 401.

item.name: {{baseUrl}}/Patient?_format=xml (no auth, format checked before auth â†’ 406)
Conditional Create
item.description: Tests FHIR R5 conditional create (Â§11.4.1.1) via the If-None-Exist header. Seeds a patient with a unique identifier (stored in `condIdentifier`). A second POST with If-None-Exist matching that identifier returns 200 with the existing resource â€” no duplicate is created. Two seeds sharing the same family name followed by a conditional create with that name returns 412 Precondition Failed.

item.name: $everything
item.description: Tests GET /<resource>/{id}/$everything (FHIR R5 instance-level operation). Seeds a Patient (`everythingPatientId`) and a linked Observation (`everythingObsId`), then verifies the returned Bundle contains both: the Patient with search.mode=match and the Observation with search.mode=include. Also verifies 404 for an unknown patient ID.

item.name: Seed then delete patient for $everything 410 test
Transaction / Batch Bundle
item.description: Tests POST / for FHIR R5 transaction and batch bundle processing (Â§10.2). A transaction bundle validates all entries atomically and commits or rolls back together; a batch bundle processes entries independently with per-entry status codes. A non-Bundle body returns 400. The transaction create saves its new Patient ID to `txPatientId`.

exec: pm.test('Entry response has location and ETag', () => {

_summary / _elements
item.description: Tests FHIR R5 response shaping (Â§3.3.1). Seeds a Patient with narrative text (`shapingPatientId`). _summary=true keeps only id, meta, resourceType, text. _summary=data strips text but retains clinical fields. _summary=count returns total with no entries array. _elements=x,y keeps the named fields plus the mandatory trio (id, meta, resourceType). All shaped responses carry a SUBSETTED meta tag.

exec: pm.test('Returns Bundle with total but no entries', () => {
pm.test('Has requested fields plus mandatory trio', () => {

item.description: Tests the _lastUpdated search parameter with FHIR date prefix semantics (ge, lt, eq, etc.) and partial-date period expansion. Seeds a Patient and captures its meta.lastUpdated date into `lastUpdatedDate`. Verifies ge<today> finds the seeded patient, ge2099-01-01 returns an empty bundle, and lt2000-01-01 returns an empty bundle.

item.name: $validate
item.description: Tests POST /{type}/$validate (FHIR R5 §4.9.3). Validates a resource against the fhir.resources Pydantic model without persisting it. A valid resource returns 200 with an informational OperationOutcome; an invalid resource returns 422; an unknown type returns 404. The CapabilityStatement advertises $validate for every resource type.

item.name: {{baseUrl}}/Patient/$validate (does not persist — resource absent after validate)

exec: pm.test('Returns OperationOutcome not a stored Patient', () => {
// verify the resource was not persisted

item.name: System Search
item.description: Tests GET / for system-wide search across all resource types. With no params returns an informational OperationOutcome. With ?_type=Patient returns a searchset of Patients only. Supports the same _count/_sort/_lastUpdated params as type-level search.

exec: pm.test('Entries are only Patient or Observation', () => {

item.name: Compartment Search
item.description: Tests GET /{CompartmentType}/{id}/{ResourceType} for FHIR R5 compartment search. Seeds a Patient (compartmentPatientId) and a linked Observation (compartmentObsId). Verifies that the Patient compartment returns the linked Observation, that an unlinked resource type returns an empty bundle, and that an unsupported compartment type returns 404.

item.name: Errors
item.description: Negative-path tests that verify correct error responses. Covers missing token (401), invalid token (401), wrong password (401), unknown resource type (404), and wrong Content-Type on PATCH (415). All responses are asserted to be OperationOutcome resources.

item.name: Conditional Headers
item.description: Tests for conditional read headers (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since) and Prefer: return preferences. Seeds a Patient (condHdrPatientId). ETag for version 1 is W/"1".

item.name: Prefer: handling=strict
item.description: Tests for Prefer: handling=strict on search endpoints. Unknown control parameters (those starting with _) return 400 in strict mode; non-underscore params and known control params are accepted. Defaults to lenient when the Prefer header is absent.

item.name: Security Labels
